desk.headline: HEPS down 48% to 339c as operating profit falls 44% to R852m; revenue down 2% to R13.6bn; dividend held at 383c
results: Revenue from continuing operations slipped 2% to R13.6bn, but operating profit fell 44% to R852m and HEPS almost halved to 339c (649c).
Electrical Engineering profit dropped 61% to R176m: power cable volumes fell about 20% on weak local infrastructure spending, while higher copper and aluminium prices led customers to delay orders.
Applied Electronics profit fell 30% to R358m as Middle East disruption and supply delays pushed defence shipments into the new year; a stronger rand also cut export revenue.
ICT profit fell 17% to R530m, hit by problems at a Nashua franchise, delayed enterprise contracts and lower yields on the Quince finance book.
Free cash flow was R878m and net cash R713m; the total dividend was kept at 383c (final 293c). Results include a R67m goodwill impairment.

guidance.summary: No numbers given. Reunert expects FY2027 to be a year of disciplined investment and execution, provided the economy does not weaken materially, with international growth, circuit breakers and defence as priorities.

points: CEO Anthonie de Beer and CFO Mark Kathan blamed the currency, metal prices, weak infrastructure demand and slower customer decisions.
Excluding once-off items, management put HEPS at 488c, down 25%.
About R500m of defence revenue (roughly R110m of operating profit) slipped into FY2027; the defence order book rose 25% to R2.7bn, with about R660m more won after year-end.
Management said the Nashua franchise control failures behind a R57m hit have been fixed; African Cables restructuring should save about R40m a year.
FY2027 was framed as a year of delivery: cutting costs, protecting margins and cash, and converting the order book.

watch: Whether delayed defence shipments land in FY2027 and the R3.3bn order book converts.
Cable volumes and margins if copper prices stay high and infrastructure spending stays weak.
Progress on the European fuze venture, which still needs approvals.
